top_findings.title: Five match files concatenated without deduplication: team records, standings and head-to-head double/triple count
top_findings.evidence: soccer_mcp.c:28 load_all loads all 5 CSVs; no (date,home,away) dedup anywhere (grep dedup|duplicate|seen|unique -> no hits). soccer_mcp.c:35 competition filter is substring contains(), so 'Brasileirao' also matches 'Brasileirao Historical'. Re-probe: standings{Brasileirao,2019} -> 'Flamengo-RJ — 180 pts (56W 12D 8L)' (true 90 pts, 28W 6D 4L); team_stats{Flamengo,2019} -> 135 matches; head_to_head{Flamengo,Fluminense,2019} -> 6 matches; query_matches lists the same 2 fixtures 3 times (Brasileirao, Serie A, Brasileirao Historical). Factual probe passes only because it used competition 'Serie A', which hits a single source.
top_findings.suggestion: Deduplicate on (normalised date ±1 day, normalised home, normalised away) at load time, and match competition by exact/normalised equality rather than substring.

top_findings.title: Standings merges distinct clubs whose normalised names are substrings of each other
top_findings.evidence: soccer_mcp.c:41 groups rows with contains(r[k].name,name)||contains(name,r[k].name); soccer_mcp.c:29 norm() strips the '-XX' state suffix, so 'Atletico-MG' and 'Atletico-PR' both normalise to 'atletico'. Re-probe: query_matches{team:Atletico,Brasileirao,2019} returns 38 Atletico-MG + 38 Atletico-PR rows; standings shows a single 'Atletico-MG — 160 pts (44W 28D 42L)' = 114 games for one club.
top_findings.suggestion: Key standings rows on an exact canonical team name (with an explicit alias table), not bidirectional substring containment.
